findings.title: basedOn.pttV9.fx6Intent is not a quotation of live v9 but an ALTERED one: it drops 66% of the intent and substitutes a terminal period for v9's colon, manufacturing a sentence boundary the source does not have
findings.measured: Live v9's FX-6 intent is 716 characters; the subject's fx6Intent is 245. Tested by == (false), then substring (FALSE), then prefix (FALSE). The two strings agree for exactly 244 characters and diverge at index 245: live has ':' opening the enumeration 'COMPLETED-BEFORE-REVOCATION, ...', the subject has '.'. 471 characters are dropped.
findings.whyTheAlterationMattersMoreThanTheLength: A truncation under-informs; an altered quotation misinforms. Because the substituted period closes the sentence, the field reads as a complete statement of v9's intent rather than as an excerpt, and a reader has no signal that anything follows. The subject is therefore not a substring of the source it names — it asserts a sentence v9 does not contain.

findings.howThisGradesAgainstThePrecedingVerdicts: Three tests governed the FC-RO observation and the FX-5 v1 rejection. (1) Does the dropped material survive elsewhere? HERE it LARGELY DOES — three of the five dropped elements survive substantively, which is a better result than FX-5 v1, where the raceSemantics assert vanished entirely. (2) Is it a true prefix, so that nothing false is asserted? HERE IT FAILS — and this is the test FX-5 v1 PASSED and that was cited as a reason FC-RO stayed an observation. The colon-to-period substitution means the quotation is altered, not merely cut. (3) Is the artifact's primary source quotation exact? FAILS, as in FX-5 v1; fx6Intent is the only source quotation this artifact has. The finding therefore crosses on different ground from FX-5 v1, and on the sharper of the two.
findings.whyItIsNotAHouseConvention: Both permission FX corpora already ACCEPTed carry their intent field whole: permission-fx4-input-corpus.v1 has fx4Intent == live, and permission-fx5-input-corpus.v2 — accepted after v1 was rejected for a related defect — has fx5Intent == live at 543 of 543 characters and additionally added fx5Proves. This artifact departs from a convention that is already live and accepted in its own family.
findings.consequence: A fixture author reading fx6Intent as the record of the source pin would take FX-6 to require only that the wording match the ICO, with no signal that v9 additionally names the three exact wordings, forbids stating a FAILED or INDETERMINATE ICO as completed, forbids six specific undo-implying constructions, makes the denylist part of the fixture's exact bytes, and explains why the class exists. Most of that is recoverable from the artifact's other fields, but not from the field that claims to be the source.

decision.recommendation: DO-NOT-SEAL. Do not record as-is. The substance is sound and should be kept: the three ICO cases are exactly v9's, the three required wordings are v9's own, the neverStatedAsCompleted flag is placed correctly on FAILED and INDETERMINATE only, all three surfaces and the denylist are NOT-AUTHORED, and every prohibition in the dispatch is respected. A v2 that restores basedOn.pttV9.fx6Intent to the full 716-character live value, and adds fx6Proves carrying v9's 'DISCLOSURE' as the FX-5 v2 sibling does, would on these bytes carry no remaining finding known to this reviewer.
decision.summaryForCoordinator: One thing fails here and it is the field the artifact rests on, but the failure is a different and sharper kind than the one I rejected in FX-5 v1, so I want to be precise about it. fx6Intent is not merely truncated — it is ALTERED. Tested by ==, then substring, then prefix: all three false. It agrees with live v9 for exactly 244 characters and then, at index 245, substitutes a period where v9 has a colon opening the enumeration 'COMPLETED-BEFORE-REVOCATION, ...'. 471 of 716 characters are dropped, and the manufactured full stop makes the remainder read as a complete statement of v9's intent rather than as an excerpt. A truncation under-informs; an altered quotation misinforms, and this field is not a substring of the source it names. In fairness the substance fares much better here than in FX-5 v1. I searched for each dropped element and three survive properly: the three required wordings appear as requiredWordingNamed, one per state; the never-stated-as-completed rule appears as a boolean; and all six denylist constructions appear in the whatIsNotAuthored line. Two do not survive at all — v9's rationale that 'the mechanics being right does not prevent the output from lying about them', and its DISCLOSURE proves label, for which there is no fx6Proves field even though the FX-5 v2 sibling added exactly that after my earlier finding. So the three tests that governed the FC-RO observation and the FX-5 v1 rejection split differently this time: test one, survival of dropped material, LARGELY PASSES where FX-5 v1 failed it; test two, is it a true prefix asserting nothing false, FAILS where FX-5 v1 passed it; test three, is the primary quotation exact, fails as before. It crosses on the sharper test rather than the same one. Nor is this a house convention: both permission FX corpora already accepted carry their intent whole — fx4Intent == live, and fx5Intent == live at 543 of 543 after v1 was rejected for a related defect — so this artifact departs from a convention already live in its own family. Everything else verifies and should be kept. No wording golden and no denylist is authored: all three surfaces are NOT-AUTHORED on every state, denylist is NOT-AUTHORED, the six constructions occur once each and only inside the line saying they are not authored, and they are v9's own words. The three ICO cases are exactly v9's, derived from live v9 since this dispatch's attack list does not name them. The neverStatedAsCompleted placement is a genuine strength — present on FAILED and INDETERMINATE, absent from COMPLETED — which is the exact reading of v9's clause and the clearest sign the truncation was a quotation slip rather than a misreading of the class. Custody is clean: subject unmoved at b3836faf and 0444 at both samplings, four of four cited digests equal live bytes, the G09 standing confirmed at Claude ACCEPT 0/0 with no Codex verdict, the D-163 join confirms OBL-FX-AUTHORING still leftoverDesign true with owner none and FX-6 inside its fourteen, HEAD 5d5d778, required-now 26, thirty gate rows, bare integers only 0/1/26, no control bytes, SATISFIED and QUALIFIED at zero, and no recency claim anywhere so nothing can go stale.
